title: Dot product
starter:
%a   = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=0
%b   = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=1
%out = buffer 1 dtype=i32 slot=2
# out[0] = a[0]*b[0] + a[1]*b[1] + a[2]*b[2] + a[3]*b[3]
# The starter only resets out[0]. Add the loop.
%o   = shrink %out 0 shape=[]
%z   = store %o 0
%out1 = after %out %z

samples.label:
buffer slot 0 starts as [1 2 3 4]
buffer slot 1 starts as [5 6 7 8]
final contents of slot 2

buffer slot 0 starts as [1 0 0 0]
buffer slot 1 starts as [9 9 9 9]
buffer slot 2 starts as [123]
final contents of slot 2

hints: You need a `range 4`, two loads that depend on it, a product, and an accumulator.
Accumulate into the version after the reset: load and store through `shrink %out1 0 shape=[]` inside the loop, then close the loop with `end`.
The output version is then `after %out1 %e`, where `%e` is the loop's end: the reset, then the loop, as a chain.

answer.code:
%a   = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=0
%b   = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=1
%out = buffer 1 dtype=i32 slot=2
%o   = shrink %out 0 shape=[]
%z   = store %o 0
%out1 = after %out %z
%k   = range 4
%av  = shrink %a %k shape=[]
%x   = load %av
%bv  = shrink %b %k shape=[]
%y   = load %bv
%p   = mul %x %y
%o1  = shrink %out1 0 shape=[]
%cur = load %o1
%sum = add %cur %p
%s   = store %o1 %sum
%e   = end %s %k
%out2 = after %out1 %e
answer.explain: A one-element accumulator: reset to 0 once, then the k loop loads, adds a[k]*b[k], and stores back. The load is used only inside the loop, which stores into the same version, so it reads the running sum each iteration. 65536 * 65536 wraps to 0, which one test checks.
